newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico invites foreign observers to July elections.
newsitem.headline: Mexico invites foreign observers to July elections.

text.p: The Mexican government said on Saturday it was inviting foreign observers to watch key Congressional and state elections in July.

"The international presence in the federal election process this year is established, as 'foreign visitors' to whom the law offers guarantees to learn about the different forms of the organisation of the elections, since everything is transparent," top election official Jose Woldenberg said.

Woldenburg, president of the general board of the Federal Electoral Institute, also said in a statement that he had met with representatives of the European Commission and Republican and Democratic officials from the United States last week to discuss the July 6 election arrangements.

Mexicans will vote for the first time to choose a mayor of Mexico City, as well as renewing the lower house Chamber of Deputies and part of the upper-house Senate and electing several state governors.
After many years of reluctance, the government allowed international election observers into the country for the first time in 1994 for presidential elections.
The long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI), in power since 1929, has been accused of using vote fraud to retain its hold on power.
President Ernesto Zedillo won the 1994 election, which international observers called generally fair, though marred by favourable access to the media for the PRI.

The government said it would issue an invitation in Mexico and abroad to observers from other governments, legislatures, election authorities and international organisations as well as political parties and groups, academics, private individuals and non-governmental organisations.
Applications would be received at Mexican embassies and consulates until June 21.
